### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. myopathy, myofibrillar, 13, with rimmed vacuoles  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3371571)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPB8 (HGNC:30171) —DISRUPTS→ Protein aggregation and clearance (GO:0042254); Protein aggregation and clearance (GO:0042254) —LEADS_TO→ Axonal degeneration (HP:0002473); Protein aggregation and clearance (GO:0042254) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003198). Loss-of-function mutations in HSPB8 impair its role in protein quality control, leading to protein aggregation and subsequent cellular dysfunction, which manifests as axonal degeneration in neurons (disease A) and myopathy (disease B).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of specific, distinct gain-of-function mutations in HSPB8 that cause one disease while loss-of-function mutations cause the other would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a common variant (AF > 0.01) in HSPB8 associated with either disease would also challenge the rarity assumption.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting pathways involved in protein aggregation and clearance, such as those involving HSPB8, could offer therapeutic strategies for both distal hereditary motor neuronopathy type 2A and myofibrillar myopathy 13.

---

#### 2. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2L  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.778)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3371571)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPB8 (HGNC:30171) —DISRUPTS→ Autophagy (GO:0006915); Autophagy (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ Distal muscle weakness (HP:0002460); Autophagy (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuropathy (HP:0007274). Loss-of-function mutations in HSPB8 disrupt the process of autophagy. Impaired autophagy leads to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular debris, contributing to motor neuron dysfunction and ultimately manifesting as distal muscle weakness and motor neuropathy in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in HSPB8 that lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in either disease would falsify this loss-of-function hypothesis. Additionally, if mutations in HSPB8 were found to be completely absent in a significant cohort of patients diagnosed with either MONDO:0008025 or MONDO:0012096, this would also falsify the proposed link. _(variant: rs74315577)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of HSPB8 in autophagy dysfunction in both diseases could lead to the development of therapeutic strategies targeting the autophagy pathway, potentially benefiting patients with both distal hereditary motor neuronopathy type 2A and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2L.

#### 3. obsolete cerebral malformation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.487)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3371571)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPB8 (HGNC:24044) —DISRUPTS→ autophagy (GO:0006915); autophagy (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor, type 2A (MONDO:0008025); MTOR (HGNC:7476) —BINDS→ autophagy (GO:0006915); AKT3 (HGNC:377) —BINDS→ MTOR (HGNC:7476); PIK3CA (HGNC:9535) —BINDS→ MTOR (HGNC:7476); PIK3R2 (HGNC:9538) —BINDS→ MTOR (HGNC:7476); HSPB8 (HGNC:24044) —LEADS_TO→ obsolete cerebral malformation (MONDO:0016054). Haploinsufficiency of HSPB8 leads to impaired autophagy, contributing to distal hereditary motor neuronopathy type 2A. The MTOR pathway, influenced by AKT3, PIK3CA, and PIK3R2, also regulates autophagy. Dysregulation of this pathway, potentially through mutations in these related genes, could also contribute to obsolete cerebral malformation, creating a shared mechanistic overlap via autophagy.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in HSPB8 are found to be heterozygous loss-of-function variants in patients with distal hereditary motor neuronopathy type 2A, but no such variants or other pathogenic variants in the autophagy pathway are identified in patients with obsolete cerebral malformation, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying a shared mechanism involving autophagy and HSPB8 could enable the development of therapeutic strategies targeting autophagy modulation for both distal hereditary motor neuronopathy type 2A and obsolete cerebral malformation, potentially benefiting patients with these distinct neurological disorders.

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPB8 (HGNC:29648) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal calcium homeostasis (GO:0007226); CAMK2B (HGNC:1316) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal calcium homeostasis (GO:0007226); neuronal calcium homeostasis (GO:0007226) —LEADS_TO→ neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor, type 2A (MONDO:0008025); neuronal calcium homeostasis (GO:0007226) —LEADS_TO→ intellectual disability, autosomal dominant 54 (MONDO:0030920). Loss-of-function mutations in HSPB8 (causative for HMN2A) and CAMK2B (causative for ADID54) converge on the disruption of neuronal calcium homeostasis, leading to distinct but related neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** If variants in HSPB8 or CAMK2B are found to have no discernible impact on neuronal calcium homeostasis in cellular or animal models, or if mutations in these genes are identified in individuals with phenotypes completely unrelated to neurological dysfunction, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Presence of common variants (>1% allele frequency) in HSPB8 or CAMK2B in gnomAD that do not segregate with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying shared mechanisms in neuronal calcium regulation between these distinct neurological disorders could pave the way for developing unified therapeutic strategies targeting calcium signaling pathways to treat both HMN2A and ADID54.

Both pathways converge on general neuronal dysfunction, manifesting as distinct but related neurological phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in HSPB8 associated with intellectual disability, or pathogenic variants in CAMK2G associated with distal hereditary motor neuronopathy, would falsify the distinct gene-disease associations proposed here. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of HSPB8 or CAMK2G, if found to be pathogenic for either disease.)_

**How to falsify it:** The absence of loss-of-function variants in HSPB8 and MTOR in affected individuals of both disease cohorts, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways that fully explain the pathogenesis of each disease independently, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: High-frequency loss-of-function variants in HSPB8 or MTOR in general population databases like gnomAD that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic overlap through HSPB8 and MTOR could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. Modulating autophagy or mTOR signaling pathways might offer a unified therapeutic strategy for patients with either distal hereditary motor neuronopathy type 2A or macrocephaly-intellectual disability-neurodevelopmental disorder-small thorax syndrome.
